## TL;DR

This pass removes the web server’s implementation-specific restart command from a connection error, makes the macOS Hub’s server response failures easier to understand, and reconnects the recovery banner test to the production API message. The previous review’s two findings are addressed: the banner fixture now imports the exact constant thrown by `api()`, and the macOS web-view status title uses plain “Server error” wording consistent with the health-check and Hub fetch messages.

## Work and rationale

I resumed from the branch after RepoOS returned task #1212 to active. The latest stored review report identified a test that asserted a locally hard-coded string instead of the string shown to users and an HTTP-specific status title in the macOS web view.

In `src/ui-app/src/api.ts`, I extracted the unreachable-server message into `SERVER_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE` and made the fetch failure path throw that constant. The API test still simulates a rejected network request and now checks the exported production constant. The recovery banner test also uses that constant as its fixture, so the classification and rendered banner checks follow the actual copy: a future change to the API message cannot silently leave the recovery flow testing stale wording.

For macOS, the web-view status title is now “Server error (503)” rather than mentioning HTTP or an “error code.” The health-check message and the Hub summary and task-search client failures now describe the same event as the server returning an error, with the response number retained for support and debugging. The existing navigation-policy test asserts the user-facing title and guidance. I searched neighboring status-handling paths after the review finding and applied the same wording to both Hub fetch clients, where status values are passed through as visible transport failures.

I updated `docs/qa/2026-11-copy-review.md` so the written review reflects the final vocabulary and accurately describes the test coverage. I also changed the failed-load preview fixture and its component-test fixtures to import `SERVER_UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE`; this keeps the real error screen and existing error-state checks aligned with the production API copy. The scope remains user-facing copy and its assertions; protocol names used in implementation code are unchanged.

## Approaches tried

I first inspected the stored review report and compared it with the current branch diff. The earlier attempted macOS change replaced “HTTP” with “error code,” which still read like an implementation label. I followed the health-check and web-view display paths to compare how their errors reach users, then chose “server error” / “server returned an error” as the shared plain-language description while preserving the useful numeric response value.

For the web regression, I chose a shared exported constant rather than importing or invoking the Vue recovery flow from the API test. This keeps the API failure behavior directly testable and lets the banner test consume the same source of truth.

## Challenges and blockers

The review report identified the current capture as stale and showing a loading state. I added a declared Work error-state capture using the `work:failedLoad` fixture and the error panel as its highlight, so the next handoff can capture populated evidence tied to the final tree.

No device-only validation was required for these wording changes. No visible browser was opened. The required scoped RepoOS check remains the final verification step for this session.

## Key learnings

A copy assertion can look meaningful while testing only a local fixture; using a shared production constant ties the API behavior, recovery UI, and failure previews to one message. When a review identifies a user-facing wording issue, nearby callers can surface the same class of error even if their source files were not named in the finding. Review evidence must also show the completed error state and match the exact branch tree being reviewed. The response number remains useful to support staff, while the surrounding sentence can still use ordinary language.
